mcqs.question: Which of the following equations best represents a displacement (single‑replacement) reaction?
mcqs.explanation: In a displacement reaction a more reactive metal (Zn) replaces a less reactive metal (Cu) from its compound, forming ZnSO4 and elemental Cu. Options B, C and D are combination, dissociation and decomposition reactions respectively, not displacement.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes the role of relative reactivity of metals in displacement reactions?

options.A: A metal higher in the reactivity series can displace a metal lower in the series from its compound.
options.B: A metal lower in the series can displace a metal higher in the series from its compound.
options.C: Reactivity does not affect whether a displacement reaction occurs.
options.D: Only non‑metals participate in displacement reactions.

mcqs.answer: A metal higher in the reactivity series can displace a metal lower in the series from its compound.
mcqs.explanation: The reactivity series ranks metals by their tendency to lose electrons. A metal placed above another is more reactive and can replace the less reactive metal from its salt. Options B, C and D contradict this principle.

mcqs.learning_point: Use metal reactivity to predict displacement
mcqs.question: How can the metal reactivity series be used to predict whether metal A will displace metal B from its salt?

options.A: If metal A is placed above metal B in the series, displacement will occur.
options.B: If metal A is placed below metal B in the series, displacement will occur.
options.C: The reactivity series is not relevant for predicting displacement reactions.
options.D: Displacement depends only on the presence of an acid, not on the series.

mcqs.answer: If metal A is placed above metal B in the series, displacement will occur.
mcqs.explanation: A metal higher (more reactive) than another can replace the less reactive metal from its compound. Options B, C and D ignore the predictive power of the reactivity series.

mcqs.question: Which of the following reactions is a double displacement (metathesis) reaction?
mcqs.explanation: In a double displacement reaction, the cations and anions of two compounds exchange partners, as seen in the formation of NaNO₃ and AgCl. Option B is a single displacement, C is a combination, and D is a decomposition reaction.

mcqs.question: When aqueous solutions of lead(II) nitrate and potassium iodide are mixed, which observation is most likely?

options.A: A yellow precipitate of PbI₂ forms.
options.B: The solution remains clear and colourless.
options.D: The temperature of the mixture rises sharply.

mcqs.answer: A yellow precipitate of PbI₂ forms.
mcqs.explanation: Pb²⁺ ions combine with I⁻ ions to produce lead(II) iodide, which is insoluble and appears as a yellow precipitate. The other options describe phenomena not associated with this reaction.

mcqs.question: A piece of zinc metal is placed in a copper(II) sulfate solution. Which observation indicates that a displacement reaction has taken place?

options.A: The blue colour of the solution fades and reddish‑brown copper metal appears on the zinc surface.
options.B: The solution starts to boil vigorously.
options.C: No visible change occurs after several minutes.

mcqs.answer: The blue colour of the solution fades and reddish‑brown copper metal appears on the zinc surface.
mcqs.explanation: Zinc, being more reactive, displaces copper from CuSO₄, forming colourless ZnSO₄ and depositing copper metal, which removes the blue colour. Options B, C and D do not describe the characteristic changes of a displacement reaction.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements reflects a common misconception about metal reactivity with acids?

options.A: All metals react with acids at the same rate.
options.B: Metals higher in the reactivity series react more vigorously with acids than less reactive metals.
options.C: The reactivity series can be used to predict displacement reactions.
options.D: Magnesium reacts more vigorously with dilute HCl than iron does.

mcqs.answer: All metals react with acids at the same rate.
mcqs.explanation: The misconception is that every metal behaves identically with acids. In reality, reactivity varies; more reactive metals (e.g., Mg) react faster than less reactive ones (e.g., Fe). Options B, C and D are correct statements about reactivity.

mcqs.learning_point: Use metal reactivity to predict displacement
mcqs.question: Given the reactivity series Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Cu, will magnesium be able to displace copper from copper(II) sulfate solution? Why?

options.A: Yes, because magnesium is above copper in the reactivity series.
options.B: No, because magnesium is below copper in the series.
options.C: The reaction does not depend on the reactivity series.
options.D: Only if the solution is heated to a high temperature.

mcqs.answer: Yes, because magnesium is above copper in the reactivity series.
mcqs.explanation: Magnesium is more reactive than copper, so it can replace copper ions in CuSO₄, forming MgSO₄ and depositing copper metal. Options B, C and D are incorrect because they ignore the established reactivity hierarchy.
